benefits: Awarded for a maximum of 24 months, granted six months at a time
Interim review after every 6 months consisting of a progress report confirmed by the dissertation supervisor
The 24-month period can be interrupted twice; an interruption may not last longer than 6 months
At least 50 per cent of the available funding is aimed to be awarded to women
Payment exclusively by SEPA transfer (IBAN required)
eligibility: All doctoral students, including members of doctoral colleges, who are enrolled at the University of Innsbruck as regular students and registered for continuation
The dissertation must be registered, otherwise the system will not allow an application

Evidence of excellent academic success (excellent grade point average plus normal duration of study, i.e. minimum duration plus 2 tolerance semesters per study/section; exceeding the minimum duration must be justified in the curriculum vitae) or scientific achievements
A maximum of two resubmissions are possible
No employment at the University of Innsbruck is permitted during the period of the scholarship
Employment outside the University of Innsbruck of more than 15 hours per week is not permitted and leads to immediate cancellation of the grant
requirements: Formal compliance with the criteria does not imply a legal entitlement to funding

Applicants involved in the main research areas of the University of Innsbruck (research areas, research platform and centers, doctoral colleges) and/or (co-)working on project proposals are given priority if they are of equal scientific quality

Publications arising from the funded study programme, including the dissertation, must refer to the scholarship granted by the University of Innsbruck, Vice-Rectorate for Research, and state the University of Innsbruck in any affiliation

Acceptance of the scholarship is declared via LFU:online; extension for a further 6 months can be requested 4 to 6 weeks before expiry, up to a maximum of 24 months, conditional on proven dissertation progress confirmed by the supervisor
A final report (max. 2-3 pages) with the supervisor's statement must be submitted to the Vice-Rectorate for Research within four weeks of the scholarship ending
Scholarship holders must arrange their own registration with the social security system and the tax office
documents: Description of the planned dissertation project (introduction/thesis, state of relevant international research, objectives/hypotheses, originality and significance, methodology, work and time planning, national and international collaborations, ethical aspects, project-relevant literature; total length 8-12 pages)
Abstract (approx. half a page, in German, understandable for laypersons)
Letter of recommendation from the dissertation supervisor
Curriculum vitae and list of publications
For doctoral students who did not complete their undergraduate studies at the UIBK: certificate of graduation and certificates (diploma/bachelor's/master's degree certificates) of all studies
SEPA bank details (IBAN), as scholarships are paid exclusively by SEPA transfer
selection_criteria: Assessment of the diploma or master's thesis
Grade point average in the basic studies (the University recommends submitting an application only with very good grades)
Scientific achievements, for example publications, presentations and project proposals
Priority for applicants involved in the University's main research areas or (co-)working on project proposals, at equal scientific quality
At least 50 per cent of the available funding is aimed to be awarded to women
coverage: Maximum of 24 months of funding, fixed for 6 months at a time
Interim review every 6 months with a progress report confirmed by the dissertation supervisor
Two possible interruptions of the 24-month period, each no longer than 6 months
application_method: Applications must be submitted during the submission period via the Student portal LFU:online
Applications outside the submission window are not possible; the system blocks applications without continuation registration and a registered dissertation
official.application_route: Apply online via the Student portal LFU:online during the published submission period of the current tranche.
official.international_eligibility: The published criteria set no nationality restriction; eligibility is defined by enrolment as a regular doctoral student at the University of Innsbruck.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field restriction is published; priority is given at equal scientific quality to applicants active in the University's main research areas (research areas, research platform and centers, doctoral colleges) or (co-)working on project proposals.
official.research_requirement: A registered dissertation is required and the application must include a description of the planned dissertation project of 8-12 pages plus an abstract.
official.duration: Maximum 24 months, awarded in six-month blocks with an interim review after each block; the 24-month period can be interrupted twice, each interruption no longer than 6 months
official.description: The University of Innsbruck awards a doctoral scholarship as start-up, interim, bridge or final financing for doctoral candidates, with a monthly allowance of 1,150 euros for a maximum of 24 months. In line with Austrian and European science and education policy, the promotion of young academics is a key objective of the University, which aims to award at least 50 per cent of available funding to women and points applicants to external funders such as the Austrian Academy of Sciences (DOC and DOC team), TNF and third-party funded projects for further financing.
official.program_type: Doctoral scholarship conceived as start-up, interim, bridge or final funding for doctoral candidates

verification.notes: Amount confirmed on both the English and the authoritative German call page as 1,150 euros per month (updated from the 1,120 figure previously catalogued); the German version prevails in case of deviations. Submission window 24 August - 9 October 2026 and all documents, eligibility rules and conditions were read directly from the call page and the 'Process and conditions' page. Note: the 'Process and conditions' sub-page still carries an older instalment figure of EUR 1,070.00, while the current 3rd tranche 2026 call page publishes 1,150 euros.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a top-up stipend for doctoral candidates already enrolled and registered for continuation at Innsbruck, not an entry scholarship, so you must already hold a registered dissertation before the portal will even let you apply. The published tranche closed on 9 October 2026 with tranches appearing roughly three times a year, so the practical move is to prepare the full dossier now and watch for the next call expected in late 2026 or early 2027. Treat it as bridge money: the University itself points to DOC, TNF and third-party project employment as follow-on funding, and the grant is incompatible with any employment at Innsbruck.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Doctoral students already deep into a registered dissertation at Innsbruck with very good grades who need up to two years of bridge or completion financing.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm in LFU:online that you are enrolled as a regular student, registered for continuation, and that your dissertation registration is recorded, otherwise the application cannot be submitted at all

Draft the 8-12 page dissertation project description against the published structure (thesis, state of research, hypotheses, originality, methodology, work and time plan, collaborations, ethics, literature)
Write the layperson abstract in German, about half a page, as required
Ask your supervisor early for the recommendation letter and later for the six-month progress confirmations
Justify any tolerance-semester overshoot in your CV and collect evidence of publications, talks and project proposals
Have SEPA IBAN details ready and check the additional-income rules before accepting
common_rejection_risks: Applying without a registered dissertation or without continuation registration, which blocks submission in the system
Exceeding the minimum study duration without a convincing justification in the CV
Weak or only very average grades in the basic studies, which the University itself flags as a reason not to apply
A project description under the 8-12 page specification or missing the published structural elements
Missing the supervisor's recommendation letter or letting a six-month extension lapse past the 4-6 week pre-expiry window
Losing the grant by taking up employment at Innsbruck or more than 15 weekly hours elsewhere
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and any fees, health and social insurance contributions and taxes are not covered; the University's conditions state scholarship holders must register with the social security system and the tax office themselves, and the scholarship is not an employment contract.
document_audit: The abstract must be in German even though the call itself is published in English
Non-UIBK undergraduates must add the graduation certificate and certificates for every study completed, not just the highest degree
Translations are not discussed in the call, so keep originals and any certified copies together before the window opens
The supervisor letter and progress confirmations are recurring paperwork obligations, not one-off uploads
alerts: The 3rd tranche 2026 window closed on 9 October 2026; the next call is only expected in late 2026/early 2027, so there is currently no open application route
Two resubmissions are the maximum, so do not burn an attempt on an incomplete dossier
The German version of the call prevails over the English one in case of deviations
Funding from this round is expected to be awarded in December 2026 with starts as late as June 2027, which affects any parallel funding you plan
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Upload the complete dossier through the LFU:online student portal within the tranche window; acceptance and extension requests are then handled in the same portal, with progress confirmed in writing by the supervisor.

official.tuition_coverage_note: ISTA states it does not charge any tuition fees, and no application fee is required to apply to the PhD, internship and scholarship programmes.
official.funding_period: per month (gross, paid 14 times a year)
benefits: Employment by ISTA with a 5-year contract and internationally competitive salary

Gross salary of 3,053 to 3,673 EUR per month in 2026, depending on whether the student holds a bachelor's or master's degree at admission, paid 14 times a year (once per month plus double payments in June and November)
Salary raise on passing the Qualifying Exam, about 1.5 years into the degree
Financial support to attend scientific conferences and workshops
No tuition fees and no application fee
eligibility: Bachelor's or Master's degree at the time of admission; the salary level depends on which degree is held
Degree in biology, chemistry, neuroscience, mathematics, computer science, physics, data science and scientific computing, astronomy, earth science and related areas
All PhD students are required to work towards the PhD full-time
Admission through the annual ISTA PhD Call; ISTA processes applications once a year
Students apply unaffiliated and join a research group only after completing three rotations in three different research groups in the first year
Students must pass the Qualifying Exam in the second year to continue on the PhD programme and perform thesis research
requirements: Contact information of three referees who can assess academic and research performance
All documents must be submitted in English; copies of university transcripts must be provided in both English and the original language
All students making reasonable progress are fully funded until the time of their thesis defence
Applications and documents received outside the application portal are not accepted or processed
The application form must be completed using a web browser on a desktop computer; mobile browsers are not supported
documents: Statement of purpose describing past research projects, motivation, skills and background relevant to the research areas and groups selected

Answers to three additional questions (up to 5-8 lines each): preferred research groups at ISTA with reasons and order; an ISTA professor's paper the applicant would have liked to be part of, with DOI citation, key findings and personal excitement; and an inspiring group, department or institution outside ISTA
University transcripts and diplomas of all degree programmes and all years attended or currently enrolled in, including the full list of courses and grades, in English and in the original language
Contact information of three referees; reference letters must be submitted by the referees by the specified deadline
selection_criteria: Undergraduate performance overall, with a special focus on relevant field-specific courses

Reference letters from professors and senior scientists, one letter from industry acceptable but academic letters given priority; referees address analytical capabilities, technical proficiency, ability to work independently and motivation/commitment
Statement of purpose: past research experience, motivation and academic fit with this particular PhD programme
Additional relevant field-specific skills such as internships, research projects, science Olympiads, programming languages and lab techniques
Transferable skills such as communication, teamwork, previous mobility and international experience, and leadership in student organisations
Diversity, for example a woman in computer science, mathematics or physics, or an applicant who switched fields
coverage: Gross salary of 3,053 to 3,673 EUR per month in 2026, paid 14 times a year
Financial support to attend scientific conferences and workshops
No tuition fees and no application fee
5-year employment contract, with funding continuing for students making reasonable progress until the thesis defence
application_method: Create an online account in the application portal during the application period (second half of October until the deadline) and track the application through its stages
The portal is available during the application period only; applications and documents received outside the portal are not processed
official.application_route: Apply once a year through the ISTA online application portal during the call window, with three referees submitting letters separately.
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality or residency restriction is published; students come from over 50 countries and the institute brings together scientists and staff from 72 countries.
official.international_eligibility: International students are eligible; ISTA has a diverse international student population from over 50 countries and an English-speaking campus.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Seven tracks of PhD study: Biology, Chemistry & Materials, Computer Science, Data Science & Scientific Computing, Mathematics, Neuroscience and Physics; applicants hold degrees in these and related areas including astronomy and earth science.
official.research_requirement: No thesis proposal is required at application; students apply unaffiliated, complete three lab rotations in the first year and defend a thesis proposal at the Qualifying Exam in the second year. The statement of purpose and the paper-analysis question serve as the research-preparation evidence.
official.duration: All students receive 5-year employment contracts; students typically complete the programme in 4.5 to 6 years, can finish earlier in 4 or 4.5 years, or may ask for a one-year contract extension depending on the nature of the research. The programme start date is uniformly 15 September and is non-negotiable.
official.description: ISTA employs its PhD students on internationally competitive salaries with full social security coverage, charges no tuition fees and no application fee, and supports conference and workshop attendance, describing financial support for PhD students as a key priority. The programme trains broad-minded scientists through an interdisciplinary curriculum of rotations, coursework and a qualifying exam before thesis research. ISTA is an independent research institute under public law with the right to confer PhD degrees, and its working language is English.
official.program_type: Doctoral programme funded through salaried employment with the Institute (fully funded)
official.english_requirement: English-taught programme and English-speaking campus; the working language of ISTA is English.

applicant_utility.summary: This is salaried employment rather than a stipend, so the practical entry ticket is a strong transcript in one of the seven tracks plus three referees who actually submit on time. The 2027 cycle opens its portal in late October 2026 and closes sharply at 3:00 PM CET on 8 January 2027, with referee letters following on 12 January and offers decided by mid-March for a fixed 15 September start. Expect to name up to three ISTA research groups and analyse one ISTA paper by DOI, which means the group-reading work has to happen before you open the portal, not after.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent bachelor's or master's graduates in the life sciences, chemistry and materials, computer science, data science, mathematics, neuroscience or physics who want a funded, English-taught doctoral position with rotations before committing to a group.
application_readiness_checklist: Read the ISTA research group list and rank up to three groups that genuinely match your background, with reasons
Pick one ISTA paper you can discuss by DOI citation, its key finding, and why it excites you, written in your own words
Collect transcripts and diplomas for every programme and every year attended, in English plus the original language
Line up three referees early and confirm they can meet the separate 12 January 2027 letter deadline
Write a statement of purpose that is specific about technical skills and past research rather than generic motivation
Use a desktop browser for the portal and watch for the account activation email in spam folders
common_rejection_risks: An incomplete application: missing transcripts for any year or programme, or missing English versions, is treated as incomplete and not progressed further
Referees who never submit, or who use the wrong link, since review only starts after reference letters arrive
A generic statement of purpose that does not address the selected ISTA groups or technical skills
Fewer than three referees entered, which blocks submission outright
Poor alignment between the ranked research groups and the applicant's actual background
Reference letters that do not speak to analytical capability, technical proficiency, independent work and motivation
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Relocation to Klosterneuburg or Vienna, housing and daily living costs on top of the gross salary, which is taxed and paid as social-security employment rather than a tax-free grant.
document_audit: Transcripts are needed for ALL degree programmes and ALL years, including the current in-progress one, not just the final diploma
Every document must be in English; transcripts additionally need the original-language version
Combine multi-page documents into single PDFs and double-check that each upload is complete before submitting
No authentication or legalisation of certificates is needed for the online application, and you may translate documents yourself
alerts: The deadline is 8 January 2027 at 3:00 PM CET and the referee letter deadline is 12 January 2027 11:59 PM CET; late portals close and no documents are accepted outside the system
The programme start is uniformly 15 September and is non-negotiable, so do not apply if you cannot commit to that date
The 2027 portal only opens in late October 2026; before that there is nowhere to submit
Mobile browsers are unsupported for the application form
Interviews run late February to mid-March and mostly remotely, with offers accepted or declined by 15 April
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create a portal account when the call opens, complete the form and upload CV, statement of purpose, question answers and transcripts, enter three referees, then submit; the committee reviews after reference letters arrive, shortlists for March interviews, and sends offers after the final selection meeting.
